doc.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Audience reception and seeing America
summary: He is well received everywhere, at home and abroad, and thinks Americans should see their own country first.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What’s it been like visiting different parts of the country and other countries, have you done a lot of traveling and do you notice a difference in how people relate to your particular brand of music?

Oh, well I’m well received everywhere. Surprisingly, you know a lot of people haven’t heard, they’ve heard it but I guess they haven’t really been aware of my kind of thing related to having a lot of blues in it. A lot of people ask you know, “how do you play like that?” or, “what kind of sound would you call that?” or, “what sort of style is that?” But I’m pretty well received, pretty well received. And in the States it’s a nice audience. I love the audiences everywhere. A lot of people see a lot of difference in the audience, but you know a good audience is a good audience. I’ve gotten them in the States and abroad. But one thing I know too is traveling, a lot of people really don’t know how beautiful America is, have never seen the country. That doesn’t have anything to do with music, but I think culturally speaking, we really don’t know how beautiful the country is, I mean to see all the sights. There’s a lot there. A lot of people spend a lot of time going to other countries, and I think they should see their country first.
In other words, some people say they always think the grass is greener, but you find out it’s the angle of the sunlight.
